solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plastic dome attached to telescope causing confusion

indicators.note: the dome is joined on after the telescope, so the telescope's name comes first

parts.note: the Hubble is the famous space telescope
a bubble is a clear dome, as on a cockpit or a plastic shelter

explanation.surface: A clear plastic dome fixed to a telescope makes for muddle at the observatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubble-bubble, besides a hookah pipe, means a noisy turmoil or muddle, a synonym of disorder.

clue.text: It's highly charged and criminally received, though not returned

parts.note: stolen goods are hot
but can mean though, as in 'small but strong'

indicators.note: the word not is written backwards, as if sent back

explanation.surface: Something electrically live, picked up as stolen property but never handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-button issue is one so emotive and divisive that it is highly charged in debate.

clue.text: Living on the edge, divers known to have vigorous urge to blaze a trail

indicators.note: the living sits at the edges of the mixed letters, wrapping round them

parts.note: bread is slang for one's livelihood or living

indicators.note: divers in its old sense of various or assorted signals the letters of known being rearranged
vigorous suggests the letters of urge being shaken up energetically

explanation.surface: Thrill-seeking divers, famed for their urge to go further, pioneer new routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is the archaic adjective meaning sundry, not underwater swimmers; with 'vigorous' it mixes the two words together, and 'on the edge' has the livelihood wrapped round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To break new ground is an idiom for doing something pioneering, just as a trailblazer goes first.

clue.text: As in the Bible, mites slept around shelters

indicators.note: the phrase slept around shelters, or holds within it, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Biblical mites have been sleeping around under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The widow's mites in the Gospels translate the Greek lepta, tiny coins, the plural of lepton.

clue.text: An extra triple bay rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of triple bay are made strange

explanation.surface: An additional order of three Bay Rums, the toiletry or the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra or minor actor has a tiny role, the kind of part a bit player takes.

clue.text: Advise book circle on doing drugs

parts.note: a ring is a circle
on doing gives up to, as in 'what are you up to?', and drugs gives ..., slang for amphetamines

explanation.surface: A reading group is told to get its act together over its drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Two pieces share the last stretch: 'on doing' is UP TO, as in 'what are you up to?', and 'drugs' is SPEED, slang for amphetamines.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone up to speed is to brief or inform them, an idiom for giving counsel or news.

clue.text: Dreaded disease is right inside ear, one concludes

indicators.note: one comes at the conclusion, the end of the answer
the letter for right goes inside the word for ear

parts.note: lug is informal British for an ear
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A feared illness shows itself in an ear infection.
explanation.definitionFit: The lurgi (or lurgy) is a jocular British name for an imaginary infectious illness, popularised by The Goon Show.

clue.text: Beating driver who may be fuelling sales talk

parts.note: a coined word for a racing driver who makes a pit stop to refuel
patter is a salesman's glib talk

explanation.surface: A beaten driver keeps up his sales pitch while filling the tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitter-patter is the rapid light beating of rain or of a heart.

clue.text: Carpetmaker, being essential to Marxist-Leninist, got brought back by first leader of Russia

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit at the core of the hyphenated word, essential to it

explanation.surface: A rug made by a communist ideologue is restored by Russia's first leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A second hiding place confirms it: 'got brought back by first leader of Russia' means the letters also appear backwards in YELTSIN, Russia's first President.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a plant fibre from Mexican agave used to make carpets, cords and nets.

clue.text: Dry back before beginning to rub in dressing for sore old man

indicators.note: the dry-plus-rub letters go in the dressing

parts.note: a patch is a dressing put over a sore

indicators.note: the turned word comes before the next letter
the word for dry is read backwards

parts.note: to air is to dry, as with laundry

indicators.note: only the first letter of rub is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for treating a sore: let it dry, then rub in ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family, an elder, and 'old man' is slang for father.

clue.text: One squeezing a jumper on the cutie, say?

parts.note: a hugger is one who squeezes in an embrace
a mugger jumps out on victims to rob them

explanation.surface: Someone hugs a sweater while lusting after a pretty young thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutie' sounds like QT, so 'on the cutie' stands for 'on the QT', secretly; the 'say?' flags that sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugger-mugger means in secret or clandestinely, the same as the idiom on the q.t.

clue.text: Contact with non-local telephone box name

parts.note: a trunk is a large box for luggage
to call is to name, as in 'we call him Bob'

explanation.surface: A long-distance phone call made from a named telephone box.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk call is the old British term for a long-distance telephone call over trunk lines.

clue.text: Current progress

explanation.definitionFit: Going serves as an adjective for prevailing and as a noun for rate of advance or headway.

clue.text: Plumpness that is not true, nakedness turning heads

parts.note: rot is nonsense, something untrue

indicators.note: the two head letters of the word for nakedness swap places

parts.note: nudity is nakedness

explanation.surface: Claims about a fat body are false, and naked display makes people stare.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotundity is roundness of figure, a synonym for chubbiness or stoutness.

clue.text: See 2
One stops at crease, batting for both teams in innings: zero runs ultimately

parts.note: a batsman at the crease is in

indicators.note: the bisexual abbreviation goes in the innings word

parts.note: a hit, or knock, is a batsman's turn at the wicket
slang for bisexual, abbreviated to bi
O is zero and R stands for runs in cricket scoring, placed ultimately, at the end

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: a batsman stops at the crease, scores nothing, and is out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman at the crease is 'in', and an innings is a turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhibitor is a substance or agent that stops or slows a process.

clue.text: In swindle it's sold to west and east in stages

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: in a swindle one is sold a pup, a worthless item

explanation.surface: In a con, goods are sold all over the map in phases.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupae are the chrysalis forms, the resting phase in an insect's development.

clue.text: Single big blow anticipated by pub lover

indicators.note: the pub comes before the other pieces

parts.note: PH stands for public house, a pub
I is one, a single
a lander is a heavy blow in old slang

explanation.surface: A lonely drinker in a pub hopes for a big romantic gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Philander is a stock name for a lover in old drama and poetry, later the verb for flirting.

clue.text: VP once again, Government admitted

indicators.note: the government letter is let into the word for again

parts.note: anew means again

explanation.surface: A former Vice-President is back in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiro Agnew was Vice-President of the USA under Nixon until resigning in 1973.

clue.text: Instrument damage restricts doctor in backsliding University

indicators.note: the damage word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: harm is damage
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: the word in slides backwards

explanation.surface: Injury confines a medic to a failing university.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium is a reed organ, a keyboard instrument pumped by foot bellows.

clue.text: One making record that's a little light

definitions.meaning: a thin candle or wick for lighting

explanation.surface: Someone recording something that is not very heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is both a slender candle and, playfully, one who tapes or records sound.

clue.text: Home that's concerning chaplain?

parts.note: pad is slang for one's home
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: Asking whether a domestic matter concerns the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the forces' term for a military chaplain or priest.

clue.text: Reports on long Scottish snake

parts.note: booms are loud reports, as of guns
lang is the Scots word for long

explanation.surface: News about a lengthy Scottish serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The boomslang is a venomous tree snake from southern Africa.

clue.text: Dad's Army, maybe — or out-of-uniform member of platoon?

indicators.note: the soldier is stripped of his outer letters, as of his outer clothing

parts.note: a platoon is made up of soldiers

explanation.surface: Is the old home guard comedy a picture of a soldier off duty?
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a 1970s British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard, still repeated on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old film, song or show, and that vintage sitcom is an example.

clue.text: See 5
Formidable old bedder out to get sloshed?

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A fearsome old college bedder heads out for a drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedder is a Cambridge college cleaner; 'old' marks the answer as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubted is an archaic term for feared or respected, much like redoubtable.

clue.text: Provide quality for Freud neurotic repressed when reclining

indicators.note: lying back, as on a couch, so the letters run backwards
the letters are kept down inside the two words, as a repressed thought is

explanation.surface: A neurotic patient on Freud's couch hides some quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or invest someone with a quality or attribute.

clue.text: Having generated negative feedback, one trashes tranny

indicators.note: the combined pieces are fed back, read in reverse

parts.note: bred means generated or produced offspring
an ender is one who ends, finishes or wrecks something

explanation.surface: After a bad review, someone wrecks a transistor radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tranny' looks like a radio here; it is the dated slang for a cross-dresser. 'Feedback' turns BREDNEG into GENDERB.
explanation.definitionFit: A gender-bender is someone who dresses or behaves to blur sex roles, an older slang sense.
